sentences.text: An application under Section 389 read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the appeal in FIR No. 355/2017 under Sections 367/376/506/342 IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act registered at PS : Khyala, Delhi.

2. Appellant was convicted vide judgment dated 02.08.2023 and sentenced vide order dated 15.09.2023 to undergo Simple Imprisonment (SI) for One year for offence punishable under Section 342 IPC; SI for Five years and fine of Rs. 2,000/- for offence punishable under Section 365 IPC (in default of payment of fine to undergo SI for 02 months); SI for Two years for offence punishable under Section 506 IPC; RI for Twenty years and fine of Rs.5,000/- for offence punishable under Section 376(2)(i) IPC (in default of payment of fine to undergo SI for 05 months).
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 25/01/2024 at 13:32:51 3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was earlier a tenant in the premises of the Nani of the prosecutrix and has been falsely implicated on account of monetary transaction.

Though it is admitted that the FIR was registered on the date of the incident itself and the prosecutrix was also examined on the same day, but it is contended that no external marks of injury Pawan Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58428252/
1 were noticed in the MLC of the prosecutrix/victim, who was aged about 12 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also contended that no witness from the public was joined, though there were other occupants in the same building.

4. On the other hand, the application has been vehemently opposed by learned APP for the State and it is submitted that evidence of victim was found to be reliable and trustworthy as discussed in the impugned judgment.
5.
A bare perusal of record reveals that the matter was reported to the police almost immediately after the incident as well as the testimony of the prosecutrix stands corroborated by the FSL result.
Considering the evidence on record, facts and circumstances of the case, no grounds for suspension of sentence are made out.
Application is accordingly, dismissed.
Nothing stated herein shall tantamount to expression of opinion on merits of case.
ANOOP KUMAR MENDIRATTA, J JANUARY 15, 2024/
